title: Human infection with a putative novel interclade recombinant monkeypox virus: a public health warning of emerging clade Ib/IIb recombinants.
abstract: We report a putative novel interclade Ib/IIb MPXV recombinant.2. This is the first putative interclade Ib/IIb MPXV recombinant identified in China.3. Two distinct recombination events were detected by multiple algorithms.4. Routine clade-specific PCR mistyping underscores the necessity of whole-genome sequencing.To the Editor Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen with increasing human-to-human transmission.The virus is divided into two major phylogenetic clades: Clade I and Clade II (including subclades Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb), which differ markedly in virulence, transmissibility, and host adaptation.Experimental studies have consistently demonstrated a virulence gradient of Clade I > Clade IIa > Clade IIb [1].The recently emerged Clade Ib lineage, first identified in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2023, exhibits sustained human-to-human transmission and virulence exceeding that of the globally circulating Clade IIb lineage [2].Genomic analyses indicate ongoing viral adaptation during human transmission, driven by APOBEC3-mediated mutations and changes in virulence-associated genes [3].While Clade IIb was responsible for the 2022-2024 global outbreak, predominantly via sexual transmission networks, Clade Ib has increasingly spread through household and community contacts, thereby expanding opportunities for wider dissemination [4, 5].Alongside mutation and selection, homologous recombination is a major mechanism of poxvirus evolution.The recent global co -circulation of Clade Ib and Clade IIb has created conditions favorable for the emergence of Clade Ib/IIb recombinants.In December 2025, a viable interclade recombinant MPXV comprising genomic regions from both Clade Ib and Clade IIb was detected in England [6], and a closely related virus was subsequently identified in India, suggesting international spread before recognition.Here, we report the first identified case of human infection with a putative novel interclade recombinant MPXV (Clade Ib/IIb) in China, as of August 17, 2026.This finding represents the second independent interclade Ib/IIb recombination event documented worldwide (the three previously reported UK/India genomes constitute a single event) and serves as a public health warning of the potentially ongoing emergence of Clade Ib/IIb recombinants.

source_records.title: Human infection with a putative novel interclade recombinant monkeypox virus: a public health warning of emerging clade Ib/IIb recombinants.
source_records.abstract: The co-circulation of monkeypox virus (MPXV) clades Ib and IIb creates opportunities for interclade recombination, with potential implications for diagnosis, viral fitness, and public health. We investigated a 34-year-old man in Hangzhou, China, who presented with penile vesicles and a subsequent maculopapular rash in June 2026. Routine clade-specific PCR identified a Clade Ib infection; however, whole-genome sequencing of throat-swab and blister-fluid specimens revealed a putative novel Clade Ib/IIb recombinant virus. Independent DNA extraction and both metagenomic and tiled long-amplicon sequencing confirmed identical recombination regions in both specimens, with full-length amplicons covering all four major breakpoint zones. SNP-based ancestry mapping identified a Clade Ib backbone containing a central Clade IIb insertion that was interrupted by a nested Clade Ib segment. RDP analysis using seven algorithms supported two recombination events, and the inferred breakpoints were concordant with the ancestry mapping. Phylogenetic analysis assigned the Clade Ib backbone to lineage A.4.1 and the Clade IIb insertion to lineage C.1.2. The recombinant virus differed substantially from previously reported UK/India recombinants and shared no breakpoints with them, indicating an independent origin. This finding suggests that recombinants may emerge rapidly when divergent clades co-circulate and highlights the limitations of clade-specific PCR alone, underscoring the need for sustained whole-genome sequencing and genomic surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to report the first identified case of human infection with a putative novel interclade Ib/IIb recombinant monkeypox virus in China, highlighting the potential emergence of such recombinants as a public health concern.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a single instance of human infection with a putative novel interclade Ib/IIb recombinant monkeypox virus, identified in China as of August 17, 2026.
analysis.methods: Genomic analysis was conducted using multiple algorithms to detect recombination events, and routine clade-specific PCR mistyping was noted, emphasizing the need for whole-genome sequencing.
analysis.main_results: Two distinct recombination events were detected by multiple algorithms, representing the second independent interclade Ib/IIb recombination event documented globally.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret this finding as a public health warning of the ongoing emergence of Clade Ib/IIb recombinants, which may have implications for disease transmission and virulence.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This finding underscores the importance of genomic surveillance to monitor the evolution of monkeypox virus and to anticipate potential changes in transmission dynamics and disease severity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single case report, which may not fully represent the broader epidemiological context, and the evidence is based on genomic analysis, which requires further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports the first case of human infection with a putative novel interclade Ib/IIb recombinant monkeypox virus in China, identified as of August 17, 2026. The findings highlight the potential emergence of such recombinants as a public health concern, given the global co-circulation of Clade Ib and Clade IIb. The study emphasizes the need for whole-genome sequencing over routine clade-specific PCR to accurately identify recombinant viruses. Two distinct recombination events were detected, representing the second independent interclade Ib/IIb recombination event globally. The authors interpret this as a warning of ongoing viral evolution and increased transmission risks. The study contributes to the understanding of monkeypox virus adaptation and recombination, underscoring the importance of genomic surveillance. However, the study is limited to a single case report, which may not capture the full epidemiological picture.

title_zh: 人类感染一种假定的新型进化枝重组猴痘病毒:新兴进化枝 Ib/IIb 重组体的公共卫生警告。
source_body_en: We report a putative novel interclade Ib/IIb MPXV recombinant.2. This is the first putative interclade Ib/IIb MPXV recombinant identified in China.3. Two distinct recombination events were detected by multiple algorithms.4. Routine clade-specific PCR mistyping underscores the necessity of whole-genome sequencing.To the Editor Monkeypox virus (MPXV) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen with increasing human-to-human transmission.The virus is divided into two major phylogenetic clades: Clade I and Clade II (including subclades Ia, Ib, IIa, and IIb), which differ markedly in virulence, transmissibility, and host adaptation.Experimental studies have consistently demonstrated a virulence gradient of Clade I > Clade IIa > Clade IIb [1].The recently emerged Clade Ib lineage, first identified in the Democratic Republic of the Congo in 2023, exhibits sustained human-to-human transmission and virulence exceeding that of the globally circulating Clade IIb lineage [2].Genomic analyses indicate ongoing viral adaptation during human transmission, driven by APOBEC3-mediated mutations and changes in virulence-associated genes [3].While Clade IIb was responsible for the 2022-2024 global outbreak, predominantly via sexual transmission networks, Clade Ib has increasingly spread through household and community contacts, thereby expanding opportunities for wider dissemination [4, 5].Alongside mutation and selection, homologous recombination is a major mechanism of poxvirus evolution.The recent global co -circulation of Clade Ib and Clade IIb has created conditions favorable for the emergence of Clade Ib/IIb recombinants.In December 2025, a viable interclade recombinant MPXV comprising genomic regions from both Clade Ib and Clade IIb was detected in England [6], and a closely related virus was subsequently identified in India, suggesting international spread before recognition.Here, we report the first identified case of human infection with a putative novel interclade recombinant MPXV (Clade Ib/IIb) in China, as of August 17, 2026.This finding represents the second independent interclade Ib/IIb recombination event documented worldwide (the three previously reported UK/India genomes constitute a single event) and serves as a public health warning of the potentially ongoing emergence of Clade Ib/IIb recombinants.

analysis_zh.main_results: 通过多种算法检测到两个不同的重组事件,代表全球记录的第二个独立的 Ib/IIb 间重组事件。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这一发现解释为对 Clade Ib/IIb 重组体不断出现的公共卫生警告,这可能对疾病 传播 和毒力产生影响。

title: New mpox data amid an evolving outbreak.
abstract: We are four years into the global mpox outbreak with continued widespread transmission of the Clade 2b strain, and more recently transmission of Clade 1b mpox outside of sub-Saharan Africa. We have no proven therapeutics for mpox other than supportive care. Most countermeasures used during the outbreak were developed for smallpox and approved without human efficacy data for mpox.1 We are now faced with an ongoing, smouldering outbreak, with low case counts, that makes vaccine and treatment trials challenging to enrol.

title: Emergence of mpox virus clade Ib cases in Spain: a four-year surveillance study (2022-2026).
abstract: Mpox virus clade Ib emerged in Spain in November 2025, with 11 cases detected in our cohort through May 2026. The clinical presentation was predominantly mild. The emergence of clade Ib MPXV cases in Spain underscores the importance of rapid and accurate molecular surveillance for clade identification. SUMMARY: A four-year surveillance study documented the first case series of mpox virus clade Ib infections in Spain, detected in 2025-2026, and presenting with predominantly mild disease.

title: Monkeypox Virus Seroprevalence among Adults Assessed at Roadside Wellness Centers along Major Transportation Corridor, Kenya, 2025.
abstract: A critical, annotated version of Narlikar’s iconic novel about a cybervirus attack by an advanced alien species—with updated text and added material. A year before Robin Cook’s Invasion (1997)—in which an alien force activates a latent biological virus in humans—and almost a decade before Liu Cixin’s The Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy (2008–2010)—in which humanity’s scientific progress is curtailed by an alien supercomputer’s “sophon-lock”—Jayant Vishnu Narlikar’s Virus (1996) painted a similar scenario. In his novel, a cybervirus broadcast by an advanced, extraterrestrial species invades Earth and freezes its digital infrastructure: a prelude to an alien invasion. The novel, first published in Marathi, recounts how vast radio arrays on Earth intercept a seemingly innocuous message from an unknown planet orbiting Barnard’s Star. The radio signal, sent six years prior, coalesces into a cybervirus that has the potential to cause a complete digital meltdown and lead humanity into an age of chaos—an alien first strike to prevent humanity from evolving further. This book—a critical, annotated version of Virus, edited and revised by Sami Ahmad Khan—reissues Narlikar’s iconic novel with updated text and added dimensions. It includes detailed annotations that locate the technology of the text along the axis of contemporary scientific thought, as well as critical essays that focus on the literary, political, and sociocultural dimensions of the novel; essays on Narlikar’s role in India’s science and science fiction; an exclusive conversation with the author; bibliographical information on his works; and a bonus short story. Contributions by Sami Ahmad Khan, Nilam Ingole, Priteegandha Naik, Jayant V. Narlikar, and Dibyadyuti Roy.

source_records.title: Monkeypox Virus Seroprevalence among Adults Assessed at Roadside Wellness Centers along Major Transportation Corridor, Kenya, 2025.
source_records.abstract: Since 2024, Kenya has confirmed >1,000 cases of monkeypox virus (MPXV) infection. We conducted a cross-sectional serosurvey at 8 clinics along a transportation corridor in Kenya to quantify unrecognized MPXV transmission. From September 29-October 28, 2025, adults >18 years completed a questionnaire and provided blood samples tested with a serologic assay that distinguishes likely MPXV infection from orthopoxvirus vaccination. We used a modified Poisson regression to assess associations with likely MPXV infection. We compared participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to those self-reporting prior confirmed mpox cases. Of 2,896 participants, 332 (11.5%) were seropositive, including 82 (2.8%) classified as likely MPXV infection. Four participants reported prior confirmed MPXV cases, yielding a 21:1 ratio of participants with serologic evidence of MPXV infection to self-reported confirmed cases. Despite some evidence of undetected transmission, most participants lacked serologic evidence of prior orthopoxvirus exposure, indicating a large susceptible population and supporting additional vaccination and ongoing serosurveillance.

source_records.title: Virus
source_records.abstract: A critical, annotated version of Narlikar’s iconic novel about a cybervirus attack by an advanced alien species—with updated text and added material. A year before Robin Cook’s Invasion (1997)—in which an alien force activates a latent biological virus in humans—and almost a decade before Liu Cixin’s The Remembrance of Earth’s Past trilogy (2008–2010)—in which humanity’s scientific progress is curtailed by an alien supercomputer’s “sophon-lock”—Jayant Vishnu Narlikar’s Virus (1996) painted a similar scenario. In his novel, a cybervirus broadcast by an advanced, extraterrestrial species invades Earth and freezes its digital infrastructure: a prelude to an alien invasion. The novel, first published in Marathi, recounts how vast radio arrays on Earth intercept a seemingly innocuous message from an unknown planet orbiting Barnard’s Star. The radio signal, sent six years prior, coalesces into a cybervirus that has the potential to cause a complete digital meltdown and lead humanity into an age of chaos—an alien first strike to prevent humanity from evolving further. This book—a critical, annotated version of Virus, edited and revised by Sami Ahmad Khan—reissues Narlikar’s iconic novel with updated text and added dimensions. It includes detailed annotations that locate the technology of the text along the axis of contemporary scientific thought, as well as critical essays that focus on the literary, political, and sociocultural dimensions of the novel; essays on Narlikar’s role in India’s science and science fiction; an exclusive conversation with the author; bibliographical information on his works; and a bonus short story. Contributions by Sami Ahmad Khan, Nilam Ingole, Priteegandha Naik, Jayant V. Narlikar, and Dibyadyuti Roy.

It examines the seroprevalence of the mpox virus among adults assessed at roadside wellness centers along a major transportation corridor in Kenya in 2025. analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a narrative analysis of a single novel, which is not a scientific study. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that the Monkeypox virus, as depicted in the novel, has the potential to cause a complete digital meltdown and lead humanity into an age of chaos. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review presents a speculative narrative without empirical evidence or scientific consensus. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research into the biological and digital implications of the Monkeypox virus is needed, particularly in understanding its potential to disrupt global infrastructure. abstract_zh: 纳利卡标志性小说的批判性注释版本,讲述了高级外星物种发起的网络病毒攻击,并更新了文本和添加了材料。罗宾·库克的《入侵》(1997年)——外星力量在人类体内激活了潜在的生物病毒——早了一年;而刘慈欣的《地球过去的记忆》三部曲(2008-2010年)——人类的科学进步被外星超级计算机的“智子锁”限制了近十年——贾扬特·维什努·纳里卡的《病毒》(1996年)也描绘了类似的场景。在他的小说中,一种由先进的外星物种传播的网络病毒入侵地球并冻结了其数字基础设施:这是外星人入侵的前奏。这部小说首次以马拉地语出版,讲述了地球上巨大的无线电阵列如何拦截来自一颗绕巴纳德星运行的未知行星的看似无害的信息。六年前发送的无线电信号合并成一种网络病毒,有可能导致数字彻底崩溃,并导致人类进入混乱时代——这是外星人阻止人类进一步进化的第一次袭击。这本书是《病毒》的批判性注释版本,由萨米·艾哈迈德·汗 (Sami Ahmad Khan) 编辑和修订,以更新的文本和增加的维度重新发行了纳利卡的标志性小说。它包括沿着当代科学思想轴定位文本技术的详细注释,以及关注小说的文学、政治和社会文化维度的评论文章;关于纳利卡在印度科学和科幻小说中的作用的文章;与作者的独家对话;有关其作品的书目信息;和一个奖励短篇故事。Sami Ahmad Khan、Nilam Ingole、Priteegandha Naik、Jayant V. Narlikar 和 Dibyadyuti Roy 的贡献。

title: Real-world safety assessment of Mpox Vaccine in Catalonia: Retrospective Cohort Study of Adverse Events of Special Interest and Breakthrough Infections
abstract: Abstract Mpox vaccination with the Modified Vaccinia Ankara-Bavarian Nordic (MVA-BN) vaccine has been used to protect people at increased risk of infection, but real-world safety data from Europe remain limited. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 8,039 adults in Catalonia, Spain, who received at least one MVA-BN dose between June 13, 2022 and December 31, 2024, using routinely collected primary care and linked hospital records. We looked for five prespecified adverse events of special interest (myocarditis, pericarditis, thrombocytopenia, anaphylaxis and generalized convulsive seizure) within 28 days after each dose, and described mpox infections diagnosed after vaccination. Participants were predominantly men (97.7%) and aged 26–45 years (68.0%). Adverse events were rare: fewer than five cases of pericarditis occurred within 28 days of vaccination (day 19 after the first dose), and no other event of special interest was identified in that window. Sixteen participants (0.20%; 95% confidence interval 0.11–0.32%) had a recorded mpox diagnosis after vaccination. These findings provide preliminary, region-specific reassurance about the short-term safety of MVA-BN. However, events were few, there was no unvaccinated comparison group, and the study cannot establish causality or vaccine effectiveness. Continued monitoring of vaccine safety is warranted.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the real-world safety of the Mpox vaccine in Catalonia, Spain, as safety data from Europe remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted among 8,039 adults in Catalonia who received at least one dose of the MVA-BN vaccine between June 13, 2022, and December 31, 2024, using routinely collected primary care and hospital records.
analysis.methods: The study looked for five prespecified adverse events of special interest within 28 days after each dose and described mpox infections diagnosed after vaccination.
analysis.main_results: Fewer than five cases of pericarditis occurred within 28 days of vaccination, and no other event of special interest was identified in that window. Sixteen participants (0.20%; 95% confidence interval 0.11–0.32%) had a recorded mpox diagnosis after vaccination.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings provide preliminary, region-specific reassurance about the short-term safety of MVA-BN vaccine.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform ongoing surveillance and monitoring of Mpox vaccine safety in Europe, particularly in Catalonia.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study has limited evidence due to few events, lack of an unvaccinated comparison group, and inability to establish causality or vaccine effectiveness.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 8,039 adults in Catalonia, Spain, who received the MVA-BN Mpox vaccine between June 2022 and December 2024. The research aimed to evaluate the vaccine's safety by identifying adverse events of special interest within 28 days of vaccination and describing mpox infections post-vaccination. The results indicated that adverse events were rare, with fewer than five cases of pericarditis observed and no other special interest events identified. Sixteen individuals (0.20%) had mpox diagnoses after vaccination. The study provided preliminary reassurance about the vaccine's short-term safety in the region but highlighted limitations, including the absence of a control group and the inability to establish causality. These findings contribute to understanding vaccine safety in Europe but require further investigation.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果为 MVA-BN 疫苗 的短期安全性提供了针对特定地区的初步保证。

abstract_zh: 摘要 猴痘 疫苗接种 与改良痘苗安卡拉-巴伐利亚北欧 (MVA-BN) 疫苗 已被用于保护感染风险较高的人群,但来自欧洲的实际安全数据仍然有限。我们使用常规收集的初级保健和链接的医院记录,对西班牙加泰罗尼亚的 8,039 名成年人进行了一项回顾性 队列研究 研究,这些成年人在 2022 年 6 月 13 日至 2024 年 12 月 31 日期间至少接受了一剂 MVA-BN 剂量。我们在每次给药后 28 天内寻找五种预先指定的特别关注的不良事件(心肌炎、心包炎、血小板减少症、过敏反应和全身惊厥发作),并描述了在 猴痘 后诊断的 猴痘 感染。参与者主要为男性 (97.7%),年龄在 26-45 岁之间 (68.0%)。不良事件很少见:在 疫苗接种 治疗的 28 天内(第一次给药后第 19 天)发生的心包炎病例少于 5 例,并且在该窗口中没有发现其他特别值得关注的事件。16 名参与者(0.20%;95% 置信区间 0.11–0.32%)在 疫苗接种 之后记录了 猴痘 诊断。这些发现为 MVA-BN 的短期安全性提供了针对特定地区的初步保证。然而,事件很少,没有未接种疫苗的对照组,并且该研究无法确定因果关系或 疫苗 的有效性。有必要持续监控 疫苗 的安全性。

title: Respiratory Symptoms in Patients with Mpox: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Abstract Background Monkeypox (Mpox) is a zoonotic disease caused by the mpox virus, which has posed a serious threat to global public health security, especially since the worldwide outbreak in 2022. Nevertheless, current studies on the respiratory symptoms of Mpox remain limited. This analysis aims to estimate the pooled prevalence and explore sources of heterogeneity. Methods We searched PubMed, Embase, and other databases for Mpox studies published up to December 2024. The included studies were observational studies that reported at least one respiratory symptom. We employed the metaprop command in Stata software (Version 12.0) to obtain the pooled prevalence and its 95% confidence interval ( CI ). Results Finally, a total of 25 studies on the respiratory symptoms of Mpox patients were included in the analysis. The primary reported respiratory symptoms included sore throat (18%, 95% CI 13%-23%), oral lesions (17%, 95% CI 13%-22%), cough (16%, 95% CI 9%-24%), and tonsillar signs (7%, 95% CI 4%-12%). Subgroup analysis was performed according to the male proportion and geographic region of the study population, in an effort to identify the source of heterogeneity. Conclusions Sore throat is the most prevalent respiratory symptom in Mpox patients, followed by oral lesions, cough, and tonsillar signs. Further research is needed to explore potential respiratory transmission modes in mpox patients, the possibility of inducing respiratory diseases in clinical settings, and identify typical respiratory indicators that can aid in early diagnosis. This work will contribute to developing more effective and accurate prevention and control strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to estimate the pooled prevalence of respiratory symptoms in Mpox patients and explore sources of heterogeneity. The review included 25 observational studies published up to December 2024, which reported at least one respiratory symptom. The pooled prevalence of sore throat was 18% (95% CI 13%-23%), followed by oral lesions (17%, 95% CI 13%-22%), cough (16%, 95% CI 9%-24%), and tonsillar signs (7%, 95% CI 4%-12%). Subgroup analyses were conducted based on the male proportion and geographic region of the study population to identify potential sources of heterogeneity. The findings suggest that sore throat is the most common respiratory symptom in Mpox patients. The review highlights the need for further research to explore respiratory transmission modes, the risk of respiratory diseases in clinical settings, and the identification of early diagnostic indicators. These insights could aid in developing more effective prevention and control strategies for Mpox.

title: Nationwide genomic surveillance of Mpox clade IIb reveals APOBEC3-driven evolution, terminal deletions, and clade Ib introductions
abstract: The 2022–2023 global mpox outbreak highlighted the critical need for robust genomic surveillance capabilities to track mpox virus (MPXV) evolution and transmission dynamics. Building upon our established SARS-CoV-2 sequencing infrastructure, we implemented a Molecular Loop ® probe-based long-read sequencing approach using Pacific Biosciences Sequel II technology for comprehensive MPXV genomic surveillance across the United States (US). From August 2024 to June 2025, we generated 326 high-quality whole genome sequences from residual mpox-positive clinical specimens collected by Labcorp across all 10 US Department of Health and Human Services regions. Our analysis identified two samples containing clade Ib MPXV in January and June 2025 and captured shifting trends in clade IIb diversity, with 12 distinct lineages observed. We also identified multiple instances of large (~ 1.6–17.6 kb) deletions proximal to the inverted terminal repeats in clade IIb genomes. APOBEC3 mutation analysis indicated substantial evidence of human-to-human transmission among both clades. Further, we observed significantly higher APOBEC3-associated SNPs per kilobase ( P < 0.001) in clade IIb genomic variable regions relative to their central conserved region. Our assay exhibited strong reproducibility across biological replicates from individual patients and accuracy was confirmed via parallel sequencing of select specimens by US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) using metagenomic sequencing. We also demonstrated via custom simulation that our assay discriminates all known MPXV clades and lineages, including those we have not observed in the US. Our integrated nationwide surveillance system facilitates real-time genomic tracking of outbreak evolution, with demonstrated capacity across SARS-CoV-2 and MPXV, positioning this platform for rapid deployment during future pathogen emergence.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 从 2024 年 8 月到 2025 年 6 月,我们从 Labcorp 在美国卫生与公众服务部所有 10 个地区收集的残留 猴痘 阳性临床标本中生成了 326 个高质量的完整 基因组 序列。

From August 2024 to June 2025, we generated 326 high-quality whole genome sequences from residual mpox-positive clinical specimens collected by Labcorp across all 10 US Department of Health and Human Services regions. Our analysis identified two samples containing clade Ib MPXV in January and June 2025 and captured shifting trends in clade IIb diversity, with 12 distinct lineages observed. We also identified multiple instances of large (~ 1.6–17.6 kb) deletions proximal to the inverted terminal repeats in clade IIb genomes. APOBEC3 mutation analysis indicated substantial evidence of human-to-human transmission among both clades. Further, we observed significantly higher APOBEC3-associated SNPs per kilobase ( P < 0.001) in clade IIb genomic variable regions relative to their central conserved region. Our assay exhibited strong reproducibility across biological replicates from individual patients and accuracy was confirmed via parallel sequencing of select specimens by US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) using metagenomic sequencing. We also demonstrated via custom simulation that our assay discriminates all known MPXV clades and lineages, including those we have not observed in the US. Our integrated nationwide surveillance system facilitates real-time genomic tracking of outbreak evolution, with demonstrated capacity across SARS-CoV-2 and MPXV, positioning this platform for rapid deployment during future pathogen emergence.
abstract_zh: 2022-2023 年全球 猴痘 暴发 强调了对强大的 基因组监测 功能的迫切需求,以跟踪 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) 进化 和 传播 动态。在我们已建立的 SARS-CoV-2 测序基础设施的基础上,我们使用 Pacific Biosciences Sequel II 技术实施了基于 Molecular Loop ® 探针的长读长测序方法,以在美国 (US) 进行全面的 MPXV 基因组监测。从 2024 年 8 月到 2025 年 6 月,我们从 Labcorp 在美国卫生与公众服务部所有 10 个地区收集的残留 猴痘 阳性临床标本中生成了 326 个高质量的完整 基因组 序列。我们的分析在 2025 年 1 月和 6 月鉴定了两个含有进化枝 Ib MPXV 的样本,并捕获了进化枝 IIb 多样性的变化趋势,观察到了 12 个不同的谱系。我们还在进化枝 IIb 基因组 中的反向末端重复序列附近发现了多个大(约 1.6-17.6 kb)缺失的实例。APOBEC3 突变 分析表明两个进化枝之间存在人与人之间的 传播 的大量证据。此外,我们观察到,相对于中央保守区,进化枝 IIb 基因组可变区中每千碱基的 APOBEC3 相关 SNP 显着更高(P < 0.001)。我们的检测在个体患者的生物重复中表现出很强的重现性,并且美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 使用宏基因组测序对选定样本进行并行测序,从而证实了准确性。我们还通过定制模拟证明,我们的检测可以区分所有已知的 MPXV 进化枝和谱系,包括我们在美国未观察到的那些。我们的综合全国 监测 系统有助于对 暴发 进化 进行实时基因组跟踪,并在 SARS-CoV-2 和 MPXV 中展示了能力,使该平台能够在未来病原体出现期间快速部署。

title: Systematic Review of Mpox Outbreaks in Africa: Epidemiology, Transmission Dynamics, and Challenges
abstract: Pendahuluan: Mpox, yang sebelumnya dikenal sebagai cacar monyet (monkeypox), telah muncul sebagai ancaman kesehatan masyarakat yang kian berkembang di seluruh Afrika. Ancaman ini ditandai dengan meningkatnya penularan antarmanusia, perluasan cakupan geografis, serta berbagai tantangan kesehatan masyarakat yang signifikan. Tinjauan sistematis ini bertujuan untuk menyintesis epidemiologi, dinamika penularan, dan tantangan sistemik terkait wabah Mpox di negara-negara Afrika. Metode: Pelaporan disusun berdasarkan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Pencarian studi dan laporan mengenai epidemiologi Mpox, tingkat kematian kasus (case fatality rate), serta respons kesehatan masyarakat dilakukan melalui PubMed dan sumber-sumber kelembagaan, termasuk WHO dan Africa CDC. Rentang waktu publikasi yang disertakan adalah 1 Januari 2020 hingga 31 Oktober 2024. Sebanyak enam sumber yang diterbitkan antara tahun 2022 dan 2024 dimasukkan dalam tinjauan ini. Temuan disintesis secara naratif. Hasil: WHO melaporkan 7.535 kasus terkonfirmasi di seluruh Afrika dari tanggal 1 Januari hingga 6 Oktober 2024, dengan 6.169 kasus di antaranya terjadi di Republik Demokratik Kongo (RDK). Bukti dari wilayah timur RDK menunjukkan adanya penularan antarmanusia yang berkelanjutan dari klad Ib. Laporan yang ditinjau mengidentifikasi adanya kesenjangan dalam deteksi kasus, kapasitas diagnostik, dan akses terhadap vaksin. Kesimpulan: Bukti yang ditinjau mendokumentasikan terjadinya penularan antarmanusia yang berkelanjutan pada wabah-wabah tertentu, serta kesenjangan yang substansial dalam kapasitas surveilans dan respons. Penguatan surveilans laboratorium, deteksi kasus, dan akses vaksin yang adil dapat mendukung upaya pengendalian wabah. Introduction: Mpox, formerly known as monkeypox, has emerged as a growing public health threat across Africa, characterized by increasing human-to-human transmission, geographic expansion, and significant public health challenges. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the epidemiology, transmission dynamics, and systemic challenges of Mpox outbreaks across African countries. Method: Reporting was guided by PRISMA 2020. PubMed and institutional sources, including WHO and Africa CDC, were searched for studies and reports on Mpox epidemiology, case fatality rates, and public health responses. The publication eligibility window was 1 January 2020 to 31 October 2024. Six sources published between 2022 and 2024 were included. Findings were synthesized narratively. Results: WHO reported 7,535 confirmed cases across Africa from 1 January to 6 October 2024, including 6,169 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). Evidence from eastern DRC was consistent with sustained human-to-human transmission of clade Ib. The reviewed reports identified gaps in case detection, diagnostic capacity, and vaccine access. Conclusion: The reviewed evidence documents sustained human transmission in specific outbreaks and substantial gaps in surveillance and response capacity. Strengthening laboratory surveillance, case detection, and equitable vaccine access can support outbreak control.

abstract_zh: Pendahuluan:猴痘、yang sebelumnya dikenal sebagai cacar monyet(猴痘)、telah muncul sebagai ancaman kesehatan masyarakat yang kian berkembang di seluruh Afrika。Ancaman ini ditandai dengan meningkatnya penularan antarmanusia,perluasan cakupan geografis,serta berbagai tantangan kesehatan masyarakat yang signifikan.流行病学、流行病学、流行病学和非洲国家的 猴痘 系统都是如此。方法:Pelaporan disusun berdasarkan pedoman PRISMA 2020. Pencarian 研究和 laporan mengenai 流行病学 猴痘、tingkat kematian kasus(病死率)、serta 响应 kesehatan masyarakat dilakukan melalui PubMed 和 sumber-sumber kelembagaan、termasuk世界卫生组织和非洲疾病预防控制中心。出租时间为 2020 年 1 月 1 日,2024 年 10 月 31 日。为 2022 年和 2024 年提供服务。Temuan disintesis secara naratif。哈西尔:世卫组织于 2024 年 10 月 6 日发布了 7.535 号非洲法令,并于 2024 年 10 月 6 日发布了 6.169 号法令。Bukti dari wilayah timur RDK menunjukkan adanya penularan antarmanusia yang berkelanjutan dari klad Ib。Laporan yang ditinjau mengidentifikasi adanya kesenjangan dalam deteksi kasus,Kapasitas diagnostik,dan akses terhadap vaksin.关键是:请注意,请确保您的安全,并确保您的安全,并提供大量的监控和响应。Penguatan surveilans 实验室、deteksi kasus、dan akses vaksin yang adil dapat mendukung upaya pengendalian wabah。简介:猴痘(以前称为猴痘)已成为整个非洲日益严重的公共卫生威胁,其特点是人与人之间的 猴痘 不断增加、地域扩张和重大公共卫生挑战。本系统综述旨在综合非洲国家的 流行病学、传播 动态以及 猴痘 暴发 的系统性挑战。方法:报告以 PRISMA 2020 为指导。PubMed 和机构来源(包括 WHO 和非洲疾病预防控制中心)检索了有关 猴痘 流行病学、病死率和公共卫生应对措施的研究和报告。发表资格窗口为2020年1月1日至2024年10月31日。其中包括2022年至2024年期间发表的六个来源。调查结果以叙述方式综合。结果:世卫组织报告2024年1月1日至10月6日非洲各地确诊病例7,535例,其中刚果民主共和国(DRC)有6,169例。来自刚果民主共和国东部的证据与 Ib 分支的持续人传人 传播 一致。审查后的报告发现了病例检测、诊断能力和 疫苗 访问方面的差距。结论:审查的证据文件维持了人类 传播 的特定 暴发 和 监测 和响应能力的巨大差距。加强实验室监测、病例检测和公平的疫苗准入可以支持暴发控制。

title: An accurate multiplex orthopoxvirus IgG panel for distinguishing vaccinated or exposed individuals from naïve individuals using machine-learning-guided feature selection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a major human orthopoxvirus (OPXV) disease in the post-smallpox-eradication era. Rapid, scalable serology that distinguishes immunologically naive individuals from those with prior OPXV vaccination or exposure is important for surveillance, outbreak response, and vaccine-program evaluation. The primary cross-sectional analysis included 229 de-identified human serum or plasma specimens provisionally classified as naive (born after 1972; n = 116), presumed smallpox-vaccinated (born before 1972; n = 89), or MPXV-exposed/infected (n = 24). Median fluorescence intensity (MFI) values were analyzed using partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) and Boruta/Random Forest feature selection under stratified nested cross-validation. Performance metrics included apparent sensitivity, apparent specificity, overall accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), and balanced accuracy. RESULTS: The 11-antigen profile broadly separated naive specimens from presumed smallpox-vaccinated and MPXV-exposed/infected specimens. Using per-antigen cutoffs derived from the presumed naive group, the highest apparent discrimination was observed for MPXV A35R, VARV A36R, VACV A33R, and MPXV B6R. Boruta/Random Forest analysis identified a compact five-antigen signature - MPXV A35R, VARV A36R, MPXV B6R, MPXV E8L, and VACV A33R - that achieved 89.52% overall accuracy and 83.07% balanced accuracy for three-class discrimination and 96.51% overall accuracy with 96.46% balanced accuracy for binary discrimination (naive vs. CONCLUSIONS: The selected five-antigen profile yielded 96.51% binary classification accuracy against the supplied cohort labels but does not establish clinical differentiation between vaccination and infection.

abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘,由猴痘病毒(MPXV)引起,已成为后天花根除时代的主要人类正痘病毒(OPXV)疾病。快速、可扩展的 血清学 可将免疫学上未接触过的个体与先前患有 OPXV 疫苗接种 或暴露的个体区分开来,这对于 监测、暴发 反应和 疫苗 程序评估非常重要。主要横断面分析包括 229 份未识别的人类血清或血浆样本,暂时分类为幼稚样本(1972 年之后出生;n = 116)、推测接种过天花疫苗的样本(1972 年之前出生;n = 89)或 MPXV 暴露/感染样本(n = 24)。使用偏最小二乘判别分析 (PLS-DA) 和分层嵌套交叉验证下的 Boruta/随机森林特征选择来分析中位荧光强度 (MFI) 值。性能指标包括表观灵敏度、表观特异性、总体准确性、受试者工作特征 (ROC) 曲线下面积 (AUC) 和平衡准确性。结果:11 种抗原谱将原始样本与假定的天花疫苗接种样本和 MPXV 暴露/感染样本大致区分开来。使用来自假定的初始组的每个抗原截止值,观察到 MPXV A35R、VARV A36R、VACV A33R 和 MPXV B6R 的最高明显区分度。Boruta/Random Forest 分析确定了一个紧凑的五抗原特征 - MPXV A35R、VARV A36R、MPXV B6R、MPXV E8L 和 VACV A33R - 三类鉴别的总体准确度为 89.52%,平衡准确度为 83.07%,二元鉴别的总体准确度为 96.51%,平衡准确度为 96.46%(简单与结论:所选的五抗原谱相对于提供的 队列研究 标签产生了 96.51% 的二元分类准确度,但没有建立 队列研究 和感染之间的临床区分。

title: A fractional order mpox transmission model with hygiene and vaccination pathways: Analysis and calibration to the 2024 mpox upsurge in the Democratic Republic of the Congo using weekly surveillance data from 2000 to 2024
abstract: Mpox has emerged as a public health emergency of international concern, with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) at the epicentre of sustained clade I transmission and the 2023–2024 clade Ib upsurge. We develop a seven compartment Caputo fractional order model (SHVEIQR: Susceptible, Hygiene practising, Vaccinated, Exposed, Infectious, Quarantined, Recovered) which couples direct person to person transmission with behavioural and medical intervention pathways. We establish well-posedness of the model, derive the control and basic reproduction numbers using the next generation method, and prove local and global asymptotic stability of the disease free equilibrium (DFE). A normalized forward sensitivity analysis identifies the transmission rate, quarantine rate, and, at high intervention coverage, the vaccine and hygiene efficacy parameters as the dominant drivers of the reproduction numbers. Using publicly reported weekly mpox case counts for the DRC, we calibrate the model to the artefact free accelerating phase of the 2024 upsurge (weeks 9 to 32 of 2024; the 2000 to 2024 series of 1302 weekly observations is used for data description and context, and the calibration window is a 24 week subset of that series). Using nonlinear least squares, we obtain a baseline reproduction number of 2.87 (bootstrap 95% CI [2.62,3.12]), consistent with the observed exponential growth. Numerical simulations use a fractional Adams–Bashforth–Moulton predictor corrector scheme validated against classical Runge–Kutta integration at integer order, and the fractional system is rendered dimensionally consistent by an explicit reference time scaling. We show that the memory index systematically delays and flattens the epidemic peak (these trajectories are sensitivity scenarios, the fractional order α is not identifiable from the available 24 point calibration window and is therefore not estimated), which combined vaccination and hygiene coverage of roughly 45% in each channel simultaneously pushes the control reproduction number below unity, and that quarantine scale up is, parameter-for-parameter, the single most effective lever available to public health authorities in a low vaccine access setting such as the DRC. Our results provide a transparent, data grounded, and reproducible guide for evaluating mpox control policy.

title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
abstract: Abstract Mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb caused an outbreak of >100,000 cases globally, with highest disease burden in people living with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), those with CD4 count 3 . We performed an extensive autopsy on a fatal case of mpox in a man living with advanced HIV-1, who achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution despite > 6 months antiretroviral therapy and had progressive necrotizing mucocutaneous mpox disease despite multiple prolonged mpox-targeted therapies. We quantified MPXV DNA across 76 autopsy samples from different anatomical sites and observed a high burden in skin and mucosal tissue and a lower burden in all central nervous system (CNS) tissues tested. However, we detected replication-competent MPXV in multiple CNS tissues and confirmed neuronal and glial cell infection using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. MPXV sequencing from body and brain tissues revealed widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants. This case proves that replication-competent MPXV and tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates can infect and persist in the CNS of people with advanced HIV thus informing future therapeutic design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the impact of mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb on individuals with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), as this population experiences the highest disease burden during mpox outbreaks.
analysis.study_design_and_population: An extensive autopsy was conducted on a man with advanced HIV-1 who had achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution despite over 6 months of antiretroviral therapy. The study focused on a fatal case of mpox in this individual.
analysis.methods: MPXV DNA was quantified across 76 autopsy samples from various anatomical sites, and replication-competent MPXV was detected in multiple CNS tissues using RNA-scope in situ hybridization. Sequencing of MPXV from body and brain tissues identified widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated variants.
analysis.main_results: MPXV DNA was found in high quantities in skin and mucosal tissues, while lower levels were observed in CNS tissues. However, replication-competent MPXV was detected in multiple CNS tissues, and neuronal and glial cell infection was confirmed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that replication-competent MPXV and tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates can infect and persist in the CNS of individuals with advanced HIV, highlighting a novel aspect of mpox virus pathogenesis.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results inform future therapeutic strategies for mpox, particularly in immunocompromised individuals, and emphasize the need for targeted interventions in the central nervous system.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a single case, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong due to the detailed autopsy and molecular analysis of MPXV in multiple tissues.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the impact of mpox virus (MPXV) clade IIb on a man with advanced HIV-1, who had achieved HIV suppression but poor immune reconstitution. An extensive autopsy was performed, revealing high MPXV DNA levels in skin and mucosal tissues and replication-competent virus in multiple central nervous system (CNS) tissues. Sequencing identified tecovirimat resistance-associated variants, suggesting the virus can infect and persist in the CNS of immunocompromised individuals. The findings highlight the need for targeted therapeutic strategies in such populations. The study's single-case design limits generalizability, but the detailed molecular analysis provides strong evidence of MPXV's ability to affect the CNS in advanced HIV. This case contributes to understanding mpox virus pathogenesis and informs future therapeutic approaches.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) clade IIb 对晚期人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 个体的影响,因为该人群在 猴痘 暴发 期间经历最高的疾病负担。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名患有晚期 HIV-1 的男性进行了广泛的尸检,尽管经过 6 个多月的抗逆转录病毒治疗,该男性已实现 HIV 抑制,但免疫重建不良。该研究的重点是该人的 猴痘 死亡病例。
elements_zh.methods: 对来自不同解剖部位的 76 个尸检样本中的 MPXV DNA 进行了定量,并使用 RNA 范围原位杂交在多个 CNS 组织中检测到了具有复制能力的 MPXV。对身体和脑组织中的 MPXV 进行测序,发现了广泛的 特考韦瑞 耐药相关变异。
elements_zh.main_results: MPXV DNA 在皮肤和粘膜组织中含量较高,而在中枢神经系统组织中含量较低。然而,在多个中枢神经系统组织中检测到具有复制能力的 MPXV,并证实了神经元和神经胶质细胞感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,具有复制能力的 MPXV 和 特考韦瑞 耐药相关分离株可以感染晚期 HIV 个体的中枢神经系统并持续存在,这凸显了 猴痘病毒 发病机制 的一个新颖方面。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为 猴痘 的未来治疗策略(特别是免疫功能低下个体)提供了信息,并强调了对中枢神经系统进行针对性干预的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于单个案例,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,由于对多个组织中 MPXV 的详细尸检和分子分析,证据是强有力的。

abstract_zh: 摘要 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) clade IIb 在全球范围内导致了超过 100,000 例 暴发 病例,其中携带晚期人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 且 CD4 计数为 3 的人群的疾病负担最高。我们对一名患有晚期 HIV-1 的 猴痘 致命病例进行了广泛的尸检,尽管经过超过 6 个月的抗逆转录病毒治疗,该患者仍实现了 HIV 抑制,但免疫重建较差,并且尽管多次长期进行 猴痘 靶向治疗,但仍出现进行性坏死性皮肤粘膜 猴痘 疾病。我们对来自不同解剖部位的 76 个尸检样本中的 MPXV DNA 进行了定量,观察到皮肤和粘膜组织中的 MPXV DNA 负担较高,而所有测试的中枢神经系统 (CNS) 组织中的负担较低。然而,我们在多个 CNS 组织中检测到具有复制能力的 MPXV,并使用 RNA 范围原位杂交证实了神经元和神经胶质细胞感染。对身体和脑组织的 MPXV 测序揭示了广泛的 特考韦瑞 耐药相关变异。该病例证明,具有复制能力的 MPXV 和 特考韦瑞 耐药相关分离株可以感染晚期 HIV 患者的中枢神经系统并持续存在,从而为未来的治疗设计提供信息。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在调查 猴痘病毒 (MPXV) clade IIb 对晚期人类免疫缺陷病毒 (HIV) 个体的影响,因为该人群在 猴痘 暴发 期间经历最高的疾病负担。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对一名患有晚期 HIV-1 的男性进行了广泛的尸检,尽管经过 6 个多月的抗逆转录病毒治疗,该男性已实现 HIV 抑制,但免疫重建不良。该研究的重点是该人的 猴痘 死亡病例。
analysis_zh.methods: 对来自不同解剖部位的 76 个尸检样本中的 MPXV DNA 进行了定量,并使用 RNA 范围原位杂交在多个 CNS 组织中检测到了具有复制能力的 MPXV。对身体和脑组织中的 MPXV 进行测序,发现了广泛的 特考韦瑞 耐药相关变异。
analysis_zh.main_results: MPXV DNA 在皮肤和粘膜组织中含量较高,而在中枢神经系统组织中含量较低。然而,在多个中枢神经系统组织中检测到具有复制能力的 MPXV,并证实了神经元和神经胶质细胞感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,具有复制能力的 MPXV 和 特考韦瑞 耐药相关分离株可以感染晚期 HIV 个体的中枢神经系统并持续存在,这凸显了 猴痘病毒 发病机制 的一个新颖方面。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为 猴痘 的未来治疗策略(特别是免疫功能低下个体)提供了信息,并强调了对中枢神经系统进行针对性干预的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究基于单个案例,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,由于对多个组织中 MPXV 的详细尸检和分子分析,证据是强有力的。

title: HYDRA-YOLOv10: An automated approach for detection and classification of Monkeypox skin lesion stages using YOLOv10 Adapted with Circular-Responsive Attention (CRA) and Normalization-Based Attention Mechanism (NAM)
abstract: Abstract Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease whose clinical manifestations often resemble other dermatological conditions, making accurate and timely diagnosis a challenge. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as PCR, are accurate but costly, time-consuming, and often inaccessible in low-resource environments. This study proposes HYDRA-YOLOv10, a deep learning-based architecture designed to automatically detect and classify Mpox skin lesions across five clinical stages: macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, and scabs. The model incorporates key architectural innovations, including hybrid backbone connections, extended use of the C2f module for multi-scale feature fusion, and the replacement of the SPPF module with the Circular-Responsive Attention (CRA) mechanism-designed to better capture the geometry of rounded lesions using polar-aware convolutions. Additionally, the Normalization-based Attention Mechanism (NAM) replaces conventional spatial attention, enhancing feature integration and robustness to visual variations. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s superiority over state-of-the-art approaches, achieving 95.4% precision, 94.8% recall, 95.1% F1 score, 95.5% mAP@0.5, and 83.4% mAP@0.5:0.95. These results validate HYDRA-YOLOv10 as a reliable and scalable solution for automated Mpox diagnosis, offering valuable support for clinical decision-making and public health response.

source_body_en: Abstract Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease whose clinical manifestations often resemble other dermatological conditions, making accurate and timely diagnosis a challenge. Traditional diagnostic methods, such as PCR, are accurate but costly, time-consuming, and often inaccessible in low-resource environments. This study proposes HYDRA-YOLOv10, a deep learning-based architecture designed to automatically detect and classify Mpox skin lesions across five clinical stages: macules, papules, vesicles, pustules, and scabs. The model incorporates key architectural innovations, including hybrid backbone connections, extended use of the C2f module for multi-scale feature fusion, and the replacement of the SPPF module with the Circular-Responsive Attention (CRA) mechanism-designed to better capture the geometry of rounded lesions using polar-aware convolutions. Additionally, the Normalization-based Attention Mechanism (NAM) replaces conventional spatial attention, enhancing feature integration and robustness to visual variations. title: Healthcare Workers’ Preparedness for Monkeypox Pandemic Response in SubSaharan Africa: A Rapid Review Investigating the Knowledge Gap
abstract: Background: Mpox is a zoonotic viral disease caused by an Orthopoxvirus endemic to sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), where its resurgence underscores the urgent need for improved preparedness among health care workers (HCWs). Despite the potential of a One Health approach, current implementations remain fragmented. This rapid review synthesises evidence on HCWs' knowledge, attitudes, information sources, and barriers to preparedness regarding Mpox in SSA to identify training needs and policy implications. Methods: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, PubMed and ScienceDirect were searched using MeSH terms and Boolean operators for studies published between 2000 and 2024. Studies assessing HCW knowledge, attitudes, or preparedness for Mpox in SSA with full-text availability in English or French were included; those involving non-HCW populations, conducted outside SSA, or lacking primary data were excluded. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardised template; quality was assessed using the JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical CrossSectional Studies. Results: Five studies from 388 records were included (Cameroon, Ethiopia, Nigeria, DRC; n = 1,672 HCWs). Only 46.8% of HCWs demonstrated adequate Mpox knowledge. Barriers included reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention correlated with higher knowledge levels. Conclusion: Fewer than half of SSA HCWs demonstrate adequate Mpox knowledge despite a regional case fatality rate nearly ten times the global average; positive attitudes are not translating into clinical preparedness, reflecting a critical intention-action gap; and social media dominates as an information source, underscoring the need for peer-reviewed alternatives within a One Health training framework.
journal: Journal of Clinical Virology and Translational Research

analysis.summary_en: This rapid review examines healthcare workers' (HCWs) preparedness for monkeypox (Mpox) pandemic response in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). It highlights that only 46.8% of HCWs have adequate knowledge about Mpox, despite its high regional case fatality rate. Barriers to preparedness include reliance on social media and limited access to formal training. Positive attitudes towards prevention are associated with higher knowledge levels, but these attitudes do not translate into clinical preparedness, indicating an intention-action gap. The review underscores the need for peer-reviewed information sources and a One Health training framework to address these gaps. The findings suggest a critical need for targeted training and policy interventions to improve HCWs' readiness for Mpox outbreaks in SSA.

title: Comparative Performance of CNN and HOG-LBP-Based SVM for Mpox Classification
abstract: Skin lesions caused by mpox may visually resemble those resulting from other skin diseases, making image-based classification a potential approach to support preliminary screening. This study aimed to compare the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) using combined Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) features for binary classification of mpox and other skin lesion images. The experimental dataset consisted of 224 unique original images, comprising 116 mpox images and 108 images of other conditions, including chickenpox and measles. The SVM employed a 23,250-dimensional HOG-LBP feature vector with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, whereas the CNN automatically learned visual representations from preprocessed RGB images. Both models were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold cross-validation partitions, with data splitting performed before augmentation and hyperparameter tuning conducted within the training partitions. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and specificity. The CNN achieved an average accuracy of 84.37%, precision of 88.73%, recall of 80.25%, F1-score of 84.06%, and specificity of 88.92%. Meanwhile, the SVM achieved 83.03%, 84.87%, 81.92%, 83.32%, and 84.28%, respectively. The results indicate that the CNN achieved higher performance in four evaluation metrics, while the SVM obtained slightly higher recall. These findings demonstrate that both approaches offer different classification strengths within the evaluated dataset. Nevertheless, further evaluation using independent datasets and more diverse skin lesion images is necessary to assess their generalizability before potential application in preliminary mpox screening.

title_zh: 猴痘 分类的 CNN 和基于 HOG-LBP 的 SVM 的性能比较
source_body_en: Skin lesions caused by mpox may visually resemble those resulting from other skin diseases, making image-based classification a potential approach to support preliminary screening. This study aimed to compare the performance of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) using combined Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) and Local Binary Patterns (LBP) features for binary classification of mpox and other skin lesion images. The experimental dataset consisted of 224 unique original images, comprising 116 mpox images and 108 images of other conditions, including chickenpox and measles. The SVM employed a 23,250-dimensional HOG-LBP feature vector with a Radial Basis Function (RBF) kernel, whereas the CNN automatically learned visual representations from preprocessed RGB images. Both models were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold cross-validation partitions, with data splitting performed before augmentation and hyperparameter tuning conducted within the training partitions. Performance was assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and specificity. The CNN achieved an average accuracy of 84.37%, precision of 88.73%, recall of 80.25%, F1-score of 84.06%, and specificity of 88.92%. Meanwhile, the SVM achieved 83.03%, 84.87%, 81.92%, 83.32%, and 84.28%, respectively. The results indicate that the CNN achieved higher performance in four evaluation metrics, while the SVM obtained slightly higher recall. These findings demonstrate that both approaches offer different classification strengths within the evaluated dataset. Nevertheless, further evaluation using independent datasets and more diverse skin lesion images is necessary to assess their generalizability before potential application in preliminary mpox screening.

title: Accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based nucleic acid detection for Mpox Virus a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Mpox is an emerging and re-emerging infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus (MPXV), posing an ongoing threat to global public health. Early, rapid, and accurate detection of MPXV is essential for timely diagnosis, appropriate clinical management, and effective outbreak prevention and control. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) is widely used as the reference method for MPXV nucleic acid detection. However, its dependence on specialized equipment, trained personnel, and laboratory infrastructure limits its accessibility in resource-limited settings and point-of-care testing (POCT) applications.​ In recent years, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) systems have emerged as promising molecular diagnostic platforms owing to their high specificity, programmability, rapid detection capabilities, and potential for integration with isothermal nucleic acid amplification technologies. Various CRISPR-Cas-based assays, including Cas12- and Cas13-mediated detection systems, have been developed for MPXV detection. Although individual studies have reported encouraging diagnostic performance, their findings vary in terms of sensitivity, specificity, amplification strategies, detection formats, and clinical validation methods. Therefore, a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis is needed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based nucleic acid detection methods for MPXV and to investigate potential sources of heterogeneity.

title_zh: 基于 CRISPR-Cas 的 猴痘病毒 核酸检测的准确性系统评价和荟萃分析
source_body_en: Mpox is an emerging and re-emerging infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus (MPXV), posing an ongoing threat to global public health. Early, rapid, and accurate detection of MPXV is essential for timely diagnosis, appropriate clinical management, and effective outbreak prevention and control. Quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) is widely used as the reference method for MPXV nucleic acid detection. However, its dependence on specialized equipment, trained personnel, and laboratory infrastructure limits its accessibility in resource-limited settings and point-of-care testing (POCT) applications.​ In recent years, clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) systems have emerged as promising molecular diagnostic platforms owing to their high specificity, programmability, rapid detection capabilities, and potential for integration with isothermal nucleic acid amplification technologies. Various CRISPR-Cas-based assays, including Cas12- and Cas13-mediated detection systems, have been developed for MPXV detection. Although individual studies have reported encouraging diagnostic performance, their findings vary in terms of sensitivity, specificity, amplification strategies, detection formats, and clinical validation methods. Therefore, a comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis is needed to quantitatively evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of CRISPR-Cas-based nucleic acid detection methods for MPXV and to investigate potential sources of heterogeneity.

title: Integration of Mpox Prevention and Vaccination into HIV and Sexual Health Services: A Scoping Review Protocol
abstract: Background: Mpox continues to pose challenges to public health systems, particularly regarding equitable access to vaccination, early diagnosis, and prevention services. HIV and sexual health services have played important roles in the mpox response, offering opportunities to incorporate vaccination, risk assessment, diagnostic testing, and other preventive interventions into established healthcare pathways. However, evidence concerning how these services have been integrated, their implementation outcomes, and their implications for health equity remains fragmented. Objective: To map and characterize models integrating mpox prevention and vaccination into HIV and sexual health services worldwide, and to identify reported implementation outcomes, barriers, facilitators, and equity-related implications. Methods: This scoping review will follow the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) methodological guidance. The review question and eligibility criteria will be structured using the Population–Concept–Context framework. Searches will be conducted in MEDLINE via PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, and LILACS, supplemented by grey literature searches and reference screening. Empirical studies and operational reports published from January 2022 onward will be considered without language restrictions. Two reviewers will independently screen records and extract data using a standardized instrument. Findings will be synthesized through descriptive numerical summaries, structured evidence mapping, and qualitative content analysis. Implementation outcomes will be organized using the conceptual framework proposed by Proctor and colleagues. The completed review will be reported according to PRISMA-ScR. Expected contribution: The review will identify how mpox prevention and vaccination have been operationally integrated into HIV and sexual health services, characterize the populations reached, document implementation challenges, and highlight evidence gaps relevant to sustainable and equitable service delivery.

abstract_zh: 背景:猴痘 继续对公共卫生系统构成挑战,特别是在公平获得 疫苗接种、早期 诊断 和预防服务方面。HIV 和性健康服务在 猴痘 应对措施中发挥了重要作用,提供了将 猴痘、风险评估、诊断测试和其他预防干预措施纳入已建立的医疗保健途径的机会。然而,关于这些服务如何整合、其实施结果及其对健康公平的影响的证据仍然支离破碎。目标:绘制和描述将 猴痘 预防和 疫苗接种 纳入全球艾滋病毒和性健康服务的模型,并确定报告的实施结果、障碍、促进因素和公平相关影响。方法:本次范围界定审查将遵循乔安娜·布里格斯研究所 (JBI) 的方法学指导。审查问题和资格标准将使用人口-概念-背景框架来构建。检索将通过 PubMed、Embase、Scopus、Web of Science、CINAHL 和 LILACS 在 MEDLINE 中进行,并辅以灰色文献检索和参考文献筛选。自 2022 年 1 月起发布的实证研究和运营报告将受到考虑,不受语言限制。两名评审员将使用标准化仪器独立筛选记录并提取数据。研究结果将通过描述性数字摘要、结构化证据映射和定性内容分析来综合。将使用 Proctor 及其同事提出的概念框架来组织实施结果。已完成的审查将根据 PRISMA-ScR 进行报告。预期贡献:审查将确定 猴痘 预防和 疫苗接种 如何在操作上纳入艾滋病毒和性健康服务,描述所覆盖人群的特征,记录实施挑战,并强调与可持续和公平服务提供相关的证据差距。

title: Development of Therapeutics for Orthopoxvirus and Enterovirus infections: Small Molecule Antiviral Drug Discovery and Library Generation
abstract: Endemic diseases have the potential to spread quickly and overwhelm vulnerable populations, leading to the necessity for antiviral drugs to treat infections. This work focuses on the development of antivirals for orthopoxviruses and enteroviruses, as well as compound library development. Orthopoxviruses, which include monkeypox virus (mpox), vaccinia virus, and the eradicated smallpox virus, have few approved therapies, with no antiviral drug being approved for mpox infection. The viral p37 protein is a known therapeutic target for poxvirus antivirals. Tecovirimat is a known p37 inhibitor; however, it did not effectively treat mpox infections in clinical trials. Tecovirimat contains a large hydrocarbon motif, and previous changes in this motif have retained some antiviral efficacy. We identified a series of compounds containing amide, hydrazide, and carbamide linkers with adamantane, noradamantane, and other cyclic hydrocarbon substitutions with sub-micromolar potency targeting p37. The second focus of this work was the development of antivirals targeting Enterovirus-D68 (EV-D68). EV-D68 is an upper respiratory virus associated with polio-like acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) and primarily represents a threat to children under 16. Currently, there is no vaccine or Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug to combat EV-D68 infections. We used high-throughput screening to identify a promising hit molecule that we further optimized. We identified that the target was the VP1 capsid protein. We identified candidates Jun14135 and Jun14934 having broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple strains of EV-D68. Furthermore, we identified the potential for co-therapy opportunities of Jun16934 with the EV-D68 2C inhibitor Jun6504. Finally, we look to improve the speed of preclinical development for covalent inhibitors by developing a direct-to-biology (D2B) methodology to quickly synthesize molecules for screening. D2B is being increasingly utilized by both industry and academia, primarily due to the potential to save both time and cost by using small amounts of crude reactions for use in biological assays.

title_zh: 正痘病毒 和肠道病毒感染疗法的开发:小分子 抗病毒药物 药物发现和文库生成
source_body_en: Endemic diseases have the potential to spread quickly and overwhelm vulnerable populations, leading to the necessity for antiviral drugs to treat infections. This work focuses on the development of antivirals for orthopoxviruses and enteroviruses, as well as compound library development. Orthopoxviruses, which include monkeypox virus (mpox), vaccinia virus, and the eradicated smallpox virus, have few approved therapies, with no antiviral drug being approved for mpox infection. The viral p37 protein is a known therapeutic target for poxvirus antivirals. Tecovirimat is a known p37 inhibitor; however, it did not effectively treat mpox infections in clinical trials. Tecovirimat contains a large hydrocarbon motif, and previous changes in this motif have retained some antiviral efficacy. We identified a series of compounds containing amide, hydrazide, and carbamide linkers with adamantane, noradamantane, and other cyclic hydrocarbon substitutions with sub-micromolar potency targeting p37. The second focus of this work was the development of antivirals targeting Enterovirus-D68 (EV-D68). EV-D68 is an upper respiratory virus associated with polio-like acute flaccid myelitis (AFM) and primarily represents a threat to children under 16. Currently, there is no vaccine or Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved drug to combat EV-D68 infections. We used high-throughput screening to identify a promising hit molecule that we further optimized. We identified that the target was the VP1 capsid protein. We identified candidates Jun14135 and Jun14934 having broad-spectrum antiviral activity against multiple strains of EV-D68. Furthermore, we identified the potential for co-therapy opportunities of Jun16934 with the EV-D68 2C inhibitor Jun6504. Finally, we look to improve the speed of preclinical development for covalent inhibitors by developing a direct-to-biology (D2B) methodology to quickly synthesize molecules for screening. D2B is being increasingly utilized by both industry and academia, primarily due to the potential to save both time and cost by using small amounts of crude reactions for use in biological assays.

title: Applying Target Trial Emulation in Vaccine Research: A Scoping Review
abstract: Importance: Target trial emulation (TTE) has emerged as a rigorous framework for strengthening causal inference in observational research, following the design principles of randomized clinical trials using clinical data. While TTE is increasingly applied in vaccine effectiveness and safety evaluations, its implementation, reporting practices, and alignment with regulatory standards for real-world evidence remain poorly characterized. Objective: To evaluate the methodological rigor, reporting completeness, and regulatory alignment of observational vaccine studies that emulate a target trial. Evidence Review: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2021 and August 2025 that used clinical data to assess vaccine effectiveness or safety. Eligible studies explicitly or implicitly emulated a target trial through comparative, causal inference-based designs. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data on adherence to TTE core design components (ie, eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment procedures, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrasts, and analysis plans) and alignment with regulatory real-world evidence guidance. Findings: Among 79 studies meeting inclusion criteria, 58 covered COVID-19, 19 covered influenza, and 12 covered other vaccine-preventable diseases, including herpes zoster, mpox, pneumococcal disease, human papillomavirus, and other diseases. Only 25 studies (31.6%) reported clearly documented protocols. For bias assessment and mitigation, 61 studies (77.2%) explicitly defined time zero, a key step in reducing immortal time and selection biases, while 26 studies (32.9%) used negative control to assess residual bias and only 2 studies (2.5%) used quantitative bias analysis using E-values. Despite regulatory emphasis on data credibility, systematic data quality assessments appeared in only 5 studies (6.3%). Conclusions and Relevance: In this study, methodological rigor and transparency varied widely, with documented protocols, validated operational definitions, and systematic data quality assessments all uncommon. To improve reproducibility and regulatory credibility, future research should prioritize adopting standardized TTE reporting frameworks, ensure clearly documented protocols, and incorporate data quality assessments.

Despite regulatory emphasis on data credibility, systematic data quality assessments appeared in only 5 studies (6.3%). title: Rapid Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance Informed Precautionary Public Health Action Following the 2024 Kiteezi Landfill Disaster in Uganda
abstract: Abstract Background Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) has been used to detect pathogen signals during pandemics and mass gatherings, yet its role in sudden-onset environmental disasters remains poorly understood. Following the catastrophic August 9, 2024, Kiteezi landfill collapse in Kampala, Uganda, which caused fatalities, displaced communities, destroyed sanitation infrastructure, and contaminated the surrounding environment with leachate and sewage, the Ministry of Health rapidly deployed WES to assess infectious disease risks and guide emergency public health action. Methods Between 10 and 12 August 2024, with sampling initiated within 72 hours of the collapse, we conducted a purposive cross-sectional assessment at five high-risk sites: a leachate-floodwater interface, a flowing leachate stream, two stagnant wastewater pools, and a community borehole. Moore swabs were collected at Sites A-D, and a 500 mL grab sample was collected at Site E. Concentrated extracts were qualitatively tested using commercial qPCR or RT-qPCR assays for selected enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic pathogens. The borehole sample was also cultured for Escherichia coli as an indicator of fecal contamination, and field observations documented potential exposure pathways. Results Nucleic acids from Shigella spp., Salmonella spp., non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae, enteric adenovirus 40/41, selected enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and rotaviruses A-C were detected in one or more leachate or wastewater samples. We did not detect influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, or mpox virus. In the single borehole sample, Escherichia coli and all molecular targets were not detected; this single grab-sample result does not establish that the water source was safe. Field observations identified potential exposure pathways, including unprotected contact with contaminated water, children's proximity to polluted pools, livestock access to leachate, and inadequate protection of a community borehole. The response team reported implementing precautionary measures, including water-source restrictions, household water treatment, access controls, WASH activities, animal-control measures, and enhanced clinical surveillance. These measures were implemented within the broader disaster response, with environmental surveillance findings informing risk assessment and decision-making alongside field observations and other operational information. Conclusions Rapid deployment of WES after the Kiteezi landfill disaster was operationally feasible and produced site-specific evidence of environmental microbial hazards. When combined with field observations and routine disaster-response information, these findings informed precautionary public health decision-making, including drinking-water protection and exposure-reduction measures. Although the assessment did not establish the effectiveness of these interventions in preventing infections, it demonstrated the potential value of integrating environmental surveillance into early disaster-response frameworks. Future applications should incorporate repeated environmental sampling, linked clinical surveillance, and systematic documentation of public health actions and outcomes.

title_zh: 2024 年乌干达 Kiteezi 垃圾填埋场灾难后,快速废水和环境 监测 通报了预防性公共卫生行动
source_body_en: Abstract Background Wastewater and environmental surveillance (WES) has been used to detect pathogen signals during pandemics and mass gatherings, yet its role in sudden-onset environmental disasters remains poorly understood. Following the catastrophic August 9, 2024, Kiteezi landfill collapse in Kampala, Uganda, which caused fatalities, displaced communities, destroyed sanitation infrastructure, and contaminated the surrounding environment with leachate and sewage, the Ministry of Health rapidly deployed WES to assess infectious disease risks and guide emergency public health action. Methods Between 10 and 12 August 2024, with sampling initiated within 72 hours of the collapse, we conducted a purposive cross-sectional assessment at five high-risk sites: a leachate-floodwater interface, a flowing leachate stream, two stagnant wastewater pools, and a community borehole. Moore swabs were collected at Sites A-D, and a 500 mL grab sample was collected at Site E. Concentrated extracts were qualitatively tested using commercial qPCR or RT-qPCR assays for selected enteric, respiratory, and zoonotic pathogens. The borehole sample was also cultured for Escherichia coli as an indicator of fecal contamination, and field observations documented potential exposure pathways. Results Nucleic acids from Shigella spp., Salmonella spp., non-O1/non-O139 Vibrio cholerae, enteric adenovirus 40/41, selected enteroviruses, SARS-CoV-2, and rotaviruses A-C were detected in one or more leachate or wastewater samples. We did not detect influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus, or mpox virus. In the single borehole sample, Escherichia coli and all molecular targets were not detected; this single grab-sample result does not establish that the water source was safe. Field observations identified potential exposure pathways, including unprotected contact with contaminated water, children's proximity to polluted pools, livestock access to leachate, and inadequate protection of a community borehole. The response team reported implementing precautionary measures, including water-source restrictions, household water treatment, access controls, WASH activities, animal-control measures, and enhanced clinical surveillance. These measures were implemented within the broader disaster response, with environmental surveillance findings informing risk assessment and decision-making alongside field observations and other operational information. Conclusions Rapid deployment of WES after the Kiteezi landfill disaster was operationally feasible and produced site-specific evidence of environmental microbial hazards. When combined with field observations and routine disaster-response information, these findings informed precautionary public health decision-making, including drinking-water protection and exposure-reduction measures. Although the assessment did not establish the effectiveness of these interventions in preventing infections, it demonstrated the potential value of integrating environmental surveillance into early disaster-response frameworks. Future applications should incorporate repeated environmental sampling, linked clinical surveillance, and systematic documentation of public health actions and outcomes.
abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 废水和环境 监测 (WES) 已被用来检测大流行和大规模集会期间的病原体信号,但其在突发环境灾难中的作用仍知之甚少。2024 年 8 月 9 日,乌干达坎帕拉的 Kiteezi 垃圾填埋场发生灾难性倒塌,造成人员死亡、社区流离失所、卫生基础设施被毁,渗滤液和污水污染周围环境。之后,卫生部迅速部署了 WES 来评估传染病风险并指导紧急公共卫生行动。方法 2024 年 8 月 10 日至 12 日期间,我们在塌方后 72 小时内开始采样,对五个高风险地点进行了有目的的横断面评估:渗滤液-洪水界面、流动的渗滤液流、两个停滞的废水池和一个社区钻孔。在 A-D 地点收集 Moore 拭子,在 E 地点收集 500 mL 抓样。使用商业 qPCR 或 RT-qPCR 检测对选定的肠道、呼吸道和人畜共患病原体对浓缩提取物进行定性测试。还对钻孔样本进行了大肠杆菌培养,作为粪便污染的指标,现场观察记录了潜在的暴露途径。结果 在一份或多份渗滤液或废水样品中检测到志贺氏菌属、沙门氏菌属、非 O1/非 O139 霍乱弧菌、肠道腺病毒 40/41、选定的肠道病毒、SARS-CoV-2 和轮状病毒 A-C 的核酸。我们没有检测到甲型和乙型流感病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒或 猴痘病毒。在单个钻孔样品中,未检测到大肠杆菌和所有分子目标;这个单一的取样结果并不能证明水源是安全的。现场观察确定了潜在的暴露途径,包括无保护地接触受污染的水、儿童接近受污染的水池、牲畜接触渗滤液以及对社区钻孔的保护不足。响应小组报告了实施的预防措施,包括水源限制、家庭用水 治疗、访问控制、WASH 活动、动物控制措施和加强临床 监测。这些措施是在更广泛的灾害应对范围内实施的,环境 监测 调查结果与现场观察和其他操作信息一起为风险评估和决策提供信息。结论 Kiteezi 垃圾填埋场灾难后快速部署 WES 在操作上是可行的,并产生了特定地点的环境微生物危害证据。与现场观察和常规救灾信息相结合,这些发现为预防性公共卫生决策提供了信息,包括饮用水保护和减少接触措施。尽管评估并未确定这些干预措施在预防感染方面的有效性,但它证明了将环境 监测 纳入早期灾害应对框架的潜在价值。未来的应用应包括重复的环境采样、相关的临床 监测 以及公共卫生行动和结果的系统记录。

title: mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Mechanisms of Action and Translational Progress
abstract: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
